prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D layout of the locker room as the camera wearer walks forward past a doorframe pillar on the immediate left (bright white at ~0.3–0.6 m, within arm's reach in frames 1–4) toward a central low wooden bench and a right-hand wall of lockers. In frame 1, a person in a white numbered jersey bends over in the bottom-right foreground at ~0.5–0.8 m (within the camera wearer's arm's reach) before dropping out of view, while further ahead a person in a white shirt sits on the bench at ~3.0–3.5 m (roughly 1.0–1.5 m left of two people standing by the right lockers at ~2.0–3.0 m). Across frames 1 to 5, as the camera wearer advances and tilts downward, the seated person and bench brighten as they approach from ~3.5 m to ~1.5 m below and ahead, while the person in the black shirt on the right (who faces left and looks toward the camera wearer in frame 2 before turning away) comes within ~0.8–1.0 m (arm's reach) at the bottom-right of frame 5, partially occluding the person in the green shirt standing ~0.5–1.0 m behind them facing the back lockers. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the near left doorway plane and foreground silhouettes from the receding floor and mid-ground bench, and shows the continuous decrease in distance as the wearer steps into the room. However, the depth map is unreliable in the far background (over-darkening the back locker wall and the adjacent gym area at ~4–6 m on the upper left in frames 3–4 into near-uniform black) and blurs fine boundaries such as the seated person's limbs merging into the bench surface.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and mid-ground people and objects across the locker room, tracking the seated person on the central bench (from ~3.5 m in frame 1 to ~1.5 m in frame 5) and the two standing people on the right (~2.0–3.0 m in frame 1 to ~0.8–1.8 m in frame 5, separated from the bench by ~1.0–1.5 m). It explicitly delineates items within arm's reach of the seated person on the bench surface—labeling the dark bundle to their right as a 'backpack' in frame 1 and 'handbag' in frame 5—and separates the overlapping silhouettes of the person in the black shirt (front right) and the person in the green shirt occluding the lockers immediately behind them. In frames 3 and 4, it also segments several distant people (~4–6 m away, facing away or sideways) in the upper-left background room that are partially occluded by the left partition wall and half-wall counter. Compared to the RGB image alone, segmentation makes it easier to count distinct individuals in the cluttered upper-left background and clearly marks the boundary between the two overlapping standing people on the right. However, the map is frequently unreliable in its semantic labels and temporal consistency: in frame 1 it mislabels the bending person at ~0.5–0.8 m in the bottom-right foreground as a 'bed' and the open right-hand locker doors (~1.0 m away) as a 'suitcase', in frame 3 it mislabels the near-left doorway wall (~0.3 m away) as a 'laptop', and in frame 2 it completely misses the dark bag on the bench and the foreground doorframe.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D body skeletons (yellow) and no hand skeletons (magenta) on a black background, detecting only a small subset of the people present in the scene across frames 1, 4, and 5. In frame 1, a single upright torso-and-leg skeleton appears in the upper-center corresponding to the standing person in the black shirt (~2.0–2.5 m away on the right, holding an item within their arm's reach and standing ~0.5 m in front of the person in the green shirt), while in frames 4 and 5 only the seated person on the low wooden bench (~2.0 m to ~1.5 m ahead and below the camera wearer, facing away and toward the right) is tracked via their head, torso, and right arm reaching toward the clothing on the bench. In frame 5, as the camera tilts down and rotates slightly counter-clockwise while approaching the bench, the seated person's torso skeleton tilts diagonally in the upper-left quadrant, showing their head and shoulders angled away from the camera wearer. When combined with RGB, those few detected keypoints help pinpoint the torso lean and right-arm extension of the seated person and the hip-to-ankle alignment of the standing person despite dark clothing and self-occlusion. However, the pose map is highly unreliable and incomplete on its own: it fails to detect any skeletons at all in frames 2 and 3, completely misses the close bending person in frame 1 (~0.5–0.8 m), the standing person in the green shirt across all frames, all background individuals, and every hand in the sequence.
